Letter dated 05 January from Punong Barangay Andr i J. Memorandum dated 03 January from DILG-Region I V -A Director Castilla-Go informing Secretary Mar Roxas about the releva t updates regarding the implementation of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Decision With regard to the first and second issues, we regr t to inform you that the Department cannot render a legal opinion thereto since they are the proper subjects of appeal, With regard to the third issue, please be informed that i cases where the validity of an Ordinance duly passed by the local sanggunian is being a ailed, the Department has consistently upheld the presumption of validity in favor of the 01 inance in consonance with jurisprudence that: "[t is a sett/eå rule that an ordinance enjoys he presumption of validity" (Social Justice Society (SJS), Vlac}imirAIarique T. Cabigao and Tfnifacio S Tumbokon versus Hon. Jose L. Atienza, G.R. No, 156052, February 13, 2008, citin Vera vs. Hon. Judge Arca, 138 Phil. 369, 384[1969]). In the case of "Ermica•Malate flotel and Motel Operato Association, Inc. vs. City Mayor of Manila", (20 SCRA 849). the Supreme Court was rather emphatic, thus: "Prim arily what calls for a re versal of such decision is the absence of any evidence to offset the presumption of validity that attaches to a challenged statute or ordinance. was expressed categorically by Justice Malcolm: "The presumption fs all in favor of validity. x x x The acn•on of the elected representatives of' the people cannot be lightly set aside. The councilors must, in t e very nature of things, be familiar with Che necessities of their particglar municipality and with all the facts circumstances which surround the subject and necessitate action. The local legislative body, by enacti(lg the ordinance, has in effect given notice that the regulations are essential to the well- being of the people. x x " And in San Miguel Brewery, Inc. vs. Magno, (21 SCRA' 293), it was held that: "A municipal ordinance is not subject to collateral attack. Pubj•c policy forbids collateral impeachment of legislative acts. " Finally, in "Mayor Norberto M. Mendoza vs. Abstenenc•a de Guzman, et al. G.R. Nos. 156697-98, 09 October 2007, the newly-elected mayor of Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, questioned the validity of an Ordinance enacted by the previous s t of Sangguniang Bayan on the ground that it was not deliberated on by the aforesaid legi lative body in violation of Article 107, Rule 17 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing e Local Government Code of 1991. The Supreme Court (En Banc) through an extended decis on held and we quote: "To reiterate, a petition for mandamus is not the ropey proceeding to raise the invalidity of the questioned Ordinance. It as been held that when a municipal corporation has the power to enact an ordinance but

does so in an unauthorized mode, the Ordinance' is still legally binding until judicially held otherwise. The validity of the Ordinance cannot be questioned collaterally as a matter of defense to an action under it. Whether the Ordinance was indeed a falsified decument must be resolved in a separate action. This would afford the roper parties the opportunity to prove the validity of the Ordinance in an appropriate proceeding. Until thus resolved, the Ordinance in question enjoys a presumption of validity, and petitioner as incumbept mayor is duty- bound to implement it. " In this particular case, it appears that Ordinance No. 94-2001 has neither been repealed nor invalidated by the proper court under these ircumstances, it should be accorded the presumption of valiclity like any ordinance passed b. the City of Antipolo.
